properties.description: High-entropy layered double hydroxide on carbon cloth

nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of HE-LDHs/CC
nodes.procedure: Equimolar amounts (0.45 mmol) of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, Co(NO3)2·6H2O, Mn(NO3)2·4H2O, and Cu(NO3)2·3H2O were solubilized in 35 mL of deionized (DI) water, followed by the introduction of 4 mmol ammonium fluoride and 10 mmol urea. Once the mixture reached homogeneity, the final precursor solution was sealed within a Teflon-lined reactor, along with a functionalized carbon cloth (CC), and subsequently heated to 120°C for a period of 6 h.
nodes.source_text: 4.2 | Synthesis of HE-LDHs/CC ... heated to 120°C for a period of 6 h.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Li3%-HE-LDHs/CC
nodes.procedure: 0.0675 mmol LiNO3, 0.4365 mmol Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, 0.4365 mmol Mn(NO3)2·4H2O, 0.4365 mmol Co(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.4365 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.4365 mmol Cu(NO3)2·3H2O, 4 mmol ammonium fluoride, and 10 mmol urea were solubilized in 35 mL of DI water. The mixed solution was then transferred into a Teflon-lined reactor containing a carbon cloth (CC) substrate. The hydrothermal synthesis proceeded at 120°C for a duration of 6 h. After reaction, the synthesized material was collected, extensively washed with DI water, and desiccated. This resultant specimen was designated Li3%-HE-LDHs/CC.
nodes.source_text: 4.3 | Synthesis of Li_x%-HE-LDHs/CC ... Taking Li_{3%}-HE-LDHs/CC as an example: ... desiccated. This resultant specimen was designated Li_{3%}-HE-LDHs/CC.

nodes.characterization_summary: All Li_x%-HE-LDHs/CC samples conform to hexagonal hydrotalcite structure of CoFe LDH (PDF#50-0235) with slight low-angle shift of (012) plane and almost no shift in (003) plane after lithium doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The phase structure of the undoped HE-LDHs/CC and Li_x%-HE-LDHs/CC samples with varying lithium doping contents was characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD). As shown in Figure 1b and Figure S1, all samples conform to the hexagonal hydrotalcite structure of CoFe LDH (PDF#50-0235).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows two characteristic peaks at 400-600 cm⁻¹ for E_g bending and A_{1g} stretching of M-O bonds; Li_{3%}-HE-LDHs/CC peaks shift to lower wavenumbers indicating lattice expansion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy (Figure 1d) reveals two characteristic Raman peaks for both HE-LDHs/CC and Li_{3%}-HE-LDHs/CC in the 400-600 cm⁻¹ region.

nodes.characterization_summary: HE-LDHs/CC and Li_x%-HE-LDHs/CC exhibit uniformly distributed nanosheet morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HE-LDHs/CC and Li_x%-HE-LDHs/CC samples were characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), as shown in Figures S3 and S4. HE-LDHs/CC exhibited a uniformly distributed nanosheet morphology.

nodes.characterization_summary: HE-LDHs/CC shows near-equiatomic distribution of elements; Li_{3%}-HE-LDHs/CC elemental mapping reveals uniform distribution of all five high-entropy elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The chemical composition of the samples was characterized using energy dispersion spectrum (EDS), with the results shown in Figure S3b. ... EDS testing was also performed on Li_{3%}-HE-LDHs/CC ... The elemental mapping reveals uniform distribution of all elements throughout the material (Figure 1h).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms successful lithium incorporation; Li_{3%}-HE-LDHs/CC metal contents: Mn 16.61%, Fe 23.17%, Co 19.49%, Ni 18.79%, Cu 20.34%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The metal composition of the Li_x%-HE-LDHs/CC samples was determined via inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES). The ICP-OES results confirmed successful lithium incorporation (Figure S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: Li_{3%}-HE-LDHs/CC maintains nanosheet morphology consistent with SEM results.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images clearly demonstrate that Li_{3%}-HE-LDHs/CC maintains a nanosheet morphology, which is consistent with the SEM results.

nodes.characterization_summary: Li_{3%}-HE-LDHs/CC lattice fringe spacing measured as 0.27 nm corresponding to (101) plane, slightly larger than HE-LDHs/CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images further revealed the material's lattice structure. As shown in Figure 1f, the lattice fringe spacing was precisely measured as 0.27 nm, corresponding to the (101) plane of Li_{3%}-HE-LDHs/CC.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED from [121] zone axis confirms Li_{3%}-HE-LDHs/CC exhibits single-crystal characteristics with hexagonal hydrotalcite structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron diffraction pattern (Figure 1g) acquired from the [121] crystal zone axis in the selected region confirms that Li_{3%}-HE-LDHs/CC exhibits single-crystal characteristics with a hexagonal hydrotalcite structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe 2p_{3/2} at 712.5 eV and 2p_{1/2} at 724.4 eV confirm Fe³⁺; peak shifts 0.36 eV higher vs HE-LDHs/CC. Most 3d transition metals (except Ni) shift to higher binding energies indicating enhanced oxidation states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe 2p_{3/2} and Fe 2p_{1/2} peaks, located at 712.5 and 724.4 eV, are attributed to Fe³⁺, while the two peaks at 718.4 and 732.7 eV are satellite peaks ... Compared to HE-LDHs/CC, the Fe³⁺ characteristic peak in the Fe 2p_{3/2} spectrum of Li_{3%}-HE-LDHs/CC shifted to a higher binding energy by 0.36 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Absorption edges of Mn, Fe, Co, Cu shift to higher energies indicating increased oxidation states; Ni unchanged.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) analysis was performed on the Li_{3%}-HE-LDHs/CC and HE-LDHs/CC samples. The test results indicate that the absorption edges of the Mn, Fe, Co, and Cu elements in the lithium-doped samples all shift toward higher energies.

nodes.characterization_summary: Li doping shortens Fe-O bond length and increases covalency; element-specific M-O bond modulation observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Extended X-ray Absorption Fine Structure (EXAFS) spectroscopy was employed ... Figure 2c and Table S1 reveals that lithium doping shortens the Fe-O bond length and increases the covalent character between Fe and O.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER in situ Raman shows M-O characteristic peak weakening and transformation to amorphous MOOH peaks at 1.4 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Raman spectroscopy was performed on Li_{3%}-HE-LDHs/CC. As shown in Figure S17d, as the applied voltage gradually increased, the characteristic peak intensity of M-O on the nanosheet surface gradually weakened and transformed into the characteristic peak of amorphous MOOH.
